title: Craft a Golden AMI User Data Script
description: Write a user data script that hardens an EC2 instance on first boot.
problemStatement:
## Scenario
You are building a golden AMI for a web server fleet. The AMI itself will be created from a base Amazon Linux 2023 image, but the final hardening will be applied at launch via a user data script.

### Your Task
Write a bash user data script that:
- Updates all installed packages.
- Enables automatic security updates (using `dnf-automatic` on Amazon Linux).
- Disables root SSH login.
- Enables the host firewall (`firewalld`) and allows only ports 22 (SSH) from a specific IP `203.0.113.10`, plus 80 and 443 from anywhere.
- Installs and starts the Amazon CloudWatch agent to forward system logs.

Explain in 1‑2 sentences why this script contributes to a secure golden image.
hints: For SSH, edit `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` and restart sshd.
For firewalld, add rich rules to restrict SSH source.
expectedOutput: A bash script with the described steps, plus a short rationale.
solutionCode:
#!/bin/bash
# Update all packages
dnf update -y

# Enable automatic security updates
dnf install dnf-automatic -y
systemctl enable --now dnf-automatic.timer

# Disable root SSH login
sed -i 's/^PermitRootLogin yes/PermitRootLogin no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
systemctl restart sshd

# Enable and configure firewalld
systemctl enable --now firewalld
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=ssh
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="203.0.113.10" port protocol="tcp" port="22" accept'
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=http
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=https
firewall-cmd --reload

# Install and start CloudWatch agent (simplified)
dnf install amazon-cloudwatch-agent -y
/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -a fetch-config -m ec2 -c ssm:AmazonCloudWatch-linux -s

# Rationale: This script ensures every instance is patched, protected by a firewall, and logs centrally, maintaining a consistent security baseline regardless of who launches the instance.
